transcript: Happy 100 official shows to Lost Boys today. Back again for round No. 17. And in honour of Lost Boys hitting 100 shows, here are my top five favourite moments that did not make the final cut of the musical, going in chronological order throughout the show. Starting with number one is the pre curtain speech. The Frog Brothers used to do a pre curtain speech before the start of the show to tell you to turn off your phones. It was themed like the 80s. It was ridiculous and fun, and it set the show up with a comedic tone at the top. So I get. I get why they cut it, but I miss it. I think more shows should do themed pre curtain speeches. Number two is a small single line in the first boardwalk scene, but Lucy Emerson used to have a *line as Sam ran off to the comic book shop that was a “I choose not to worry.” And Shoshana Bean's delivery of this line was hilarious every single time. And I think dramaturgically, it doesn't make sense for Lucy because she does worry a lot about her kids, but I just. I loved that delivery. And No. 3 is the inclusion of the ensemble and the flashlight choreography in Murder Capital of the world in the final version of the show. This is just a number with the Frog Brothers and Sam, and I think it does a really great job of establishing The Frog Brothers as outsiders in the world of Santa Carla. But the flashlight choreography was so much fun. I also just love this song so much. And I do love when it was longer. Moving into act 2. At number four, it's brother. Look, did brother make sense in the context of the show? No- Not at all. Is it a great song? Absolutely. And I'm so, so excited that it's going to be included on the cast album coming out Friday. I cannot wait. A little part of me will wish that they had rewritten it à la be kind, rewind. But I get why they cut it, and I'm. I'm glad we have it preserved in some capacity. And at number five, it's the war reprise and the original fight sequence. Look, the original fight sequence never really worked. I love what they ended up doing with the fight sequence and that incredible sound design in that last climax of the show. But star used to fly. Star used to fly, and I miss that. Overall, I love this show. I will go see it 17 more times. I hope it runs hundreds and hundreds of more performances. But getting to follow this incredible show during its developmental process was truly, truly accepting that sometimes you do have to kill your darlings. And those are some darlings that will always stay with me. Also, fun piece of trivia for you. The longest running vampire musical, On Broadway is currently 157 which is the Wildhorn adaptation of Dracula that played in the early 2000s So I don't know. 158 is gonna be another big one for Lost Boys.
